assessments.statement: solver.terminal_horizon_truncation: The truncation account predicts persistent sub-10 effective_horizon. In the 8 sampled controller updates it is 10 control intervals at updates 0,5,10,15,20,25 and reduces only at the two latest sampled updates, update 30 (5) and update 34 (1), where the reduction exactly equals the remaining task time (0.05 s -> 5 intervals; 0.01 s -> 1 interval). Persistent budget-driven terminal truncation is therefore not observed; the sampled horizon follows the controller receding to the terminal. Marked weakened rather than rejected because 27 of 35 updates were unsampled and budget saturation itself persists.
supporting_relevance: F450 records effective_horizon 5, below the configured 10-control-interval horizon, while F469 records 10; the pair shows horizon reduction occurs at some updates, so the proposed plans query will establish whether truncation is persistent across the run or isolated. This bears directly on the hypothesis' named mechanism (terminal-horizon truncation).

assessments.statement: controller.budget_truncated_plan_selection: The budget-limited-selection account predicts budget/iteration-limited stops. Every sampled update terminates on User_Requested_Stop with policy_stop_reason budget_best_feasible, or on Maximum_Iterations_Exceeded, and none reaches Solve_Succeeded; 29 of the 35 applied updates reused an initialization plan (selected_iteration 0) while wall time stays ~17.78 s per 0.01 s period with 35 deadline misses. This is the better-supported of the two checked accounts. The 'coordinated with reduced horizon' clause is only partially met because full-horizon sampled updates also stop on budget, so this is retention of the mechanism, not of an exact horizon coupling.
supporting_relevance: F511 (35 deadline misses), F503 (User_Requested_Stop=34), F472 (Solve_Succeeded=1), F452 (mean complete update 17.77877309145406 s against the 0.01 s control period) and F465 (first-update wall 29.352235099999234 s) indicate a saturated solve budget; the proposed query adds per-update optimization_raw_status to test budget-limited plan selection, the hypothesis' named mechanism.

check.authorization: Current frozen diagnosis request; no production change or backend execution.
expected_observations: Across the 8 sampled update_ids the recorded effective_horizon is below the configured 10 at most sampled updates.
Across the 8 sampled update_ids the recorded effective_horizon equals the configured 10 at all but at most one update.
optimization_raw_status at most sampled updates is a budget/iteration-limited stop (e.g., User_Requested_Stop), coordinated with reduced effective_horizon.
optimization_raw_status at most sampled updates is Solve_Succeeded with full effective_horizon 10.
check.proceed_if: Both hypotheses predict the same recorded holding failure, so endpoint or physical metrics cannot separate them. Only the pattern of per-update effective_horizon together with optimization_raw_status can: persistent sub-10 horizons with budget-limited stops support the truncation account; full-horizon Solve_Succeeded updates with isolated reductions (as hinted by F450 versus F469) weaken solver.terminal_horizon_truncation and leave the saturated-budget account (controller.budget_truncated_plan_selection) as the better-supported mechanism, while a mixed pattern that co-varies horizon and status would retain both without a dominant cause. The check also confirms that the holding-speed violation (F428 > F456) is not terminal-reach related (F470 reach_passed true).
check.proposal: In candidate execution 087adee8e8a24fe88e5c85fe89e638c8, does the recorded per-update effective_horizon show persistent truncation below the configured 10-control-interval horizon across the run, coordinated with budget-limited solver stops, so as to distinguish solver.terminal_horizon_truncation from controller.budget_truncated_plan_selection as the better-supported explanation of the unchanged holding-speed failure (F428 holding_max_speed_m_s 1.1750052670100422 m/s versus F456 limit 0.02 m/s)?

check.stop_if: Stop after the single evidence_query returns effective_horizon and optimization_raw_status for the selected update_ids.; If fewer than the requested updates are returned, treat unreturned samples as unavailable, never as evidence of truncation or saturation.; Do not escalate to a numerical check, backend execution or production change within this phase (max_checks=1 shared).

policy.computation: Reported separately; never substitutes for reach or holding acceptance.
policy.objective: Raw scalar objectives under different weights are not ranked.
policy.rule: Joint acceptance first; otherwise componentwise physical comparison.
policy.tradeoff: Any physical improvement accompanied by physical worsening is a trade-off, not overall improvement.

coverage.definition: Both endpoints, timestamps aligned to task sample_period_s; missing samples are unavailable, never a pass.

duration.definition: Final closed interval [task duration - window, task duration].

position.definition: Maximum sampled world tip position error in the final interval.

speed.definition: Maximum sampled world tip translational speed norm in the final interval.
Euclidean norm of tip-site translational Jacobian times recorded backend qvel, reconstructed with sealed robot.xml and qpos; no finite differencing

terminal.definition: Euclidean world tip position error at the final execution sample; sealed evaluate.reach is the outcome authority.

control_period.definition: Simulated control spacing; synchronous wall overruns do not imply skipped applied updates or injected actuator delay.

duration.definition: Simulated task horizon, separate from computation wall time.

timing.interpretation: Applied updates, initialization selections, simulated duration and measured wall time are separate facts.

spendable.reservations: Running/unknown calls are charged at reservation until sealed; included once in ledger usage.

unmet_criterion: Historical joint reach/holding acceptance is false; exact criteria are host-bound.
